title: {session}.json (session manifest)
description: Created by step 2 (create-session.sh). cc_session_id is the Claude Code session id captured at step 2 (entry-flow). pid is the OS process id of the live claude main process (resolved by find-claude-pid.sh - walks up the process tree until comm basename == claude). worktree_path / branch / base_branch are populated unconditionally - every session lives in its own worktree post-Phase-4. bump_hint is populated by step 12 and consumed by /apex-merge step 6 for the batched VERSION bump. See apex-core.md Conventions / Session manifest schema.

pid.description: OS pid of the live claude main process owning the session. Resolved at create-session.sh time via find-claude-pid.sh. NEVER set to a transient subshell pid - that would mark the session stale to sibling /apex.

cc_session_id.description: Claude Code session id captured at step 2; never overwritten

worktree_path.description: Absolute path to this session's git worktree under <repo>/.apex-worktrees/<session>/. cleanup-session.sh reads this to fork the worktree-remove branch; /apex-merge enumerates worktrees via this path.

branch.description: apex/<session> branch name created at step 2.

base_branch.description: The branch HEAD was on when step 2 created the worktree. /apex-merge step 4 merges apex/<session> back onto this branch.

bump_hint.description: VERSION bump tier classified by step 12. /apex-merge step 6 reads every merged session's hint, picks the highest tier across the batch, and runs bump-version.sh ONCE on the final integration commit. minor > patch; major is user-set only. Optional - absent on empty-diff sessions where step 12 emitted no commit.

effective_baseline_sha.description: Optional. Written ONLY when step 8 detects a mid-run baseline supersede. Post-Phase-4 the sibling-commits-during-our-run scenario cannot occur (each session has its own branch + worktree), so this field is no longer written in practice; retained in the schema for backward compatibility with manifests written before Phase 4 retirement of the mechanism.
